review_notes: I read the whole target file. I then searched the TauCeti sources for repeated proof patterns. The main match is the "least element of a gcd-closed set of moduli divides every member" argument. It appears in this file and in two other files: HeckeCharacter/Conductor.lean (conductor_dvd_iff) and RayClass/Character/SubgroupConductor/Basic.lean (rayClassConductor_dvd_iff_forall_conductor_dvd). I checked that Modulus.lean has no existing helper (the wellFounded_dvd_and_ne uses are all inline). I did not compile the proposed lemma. The membership proofs in the three rewrites would need `show`/`unfold` to see through the `min` definition. Other parts of the file showed no non-trivial repetition: the two uses of `exists_raySubgroup_le_of_isOpen U.toSubgroup U.isOpen` are only a trivial restatement, and the x/x⁻¹ symmetry in the congruence-neighbourhood proof is already factored into `hfin`.

findings.problem: The reverse direction repeats a generic argument: if a set of moduli is closed under gcd, its well-founded minimum divides every member. The proof takes the gcd of the minimum and the member, applies `not_lt_min`, deduces `gcd = min`, and concludes with `gcd_dvd_right`. The same four lines appear, with only the set changed, in `HeckeCharacter.conductor_dvd_iff` (HeckeCharacter/Conductor.lean) and in `Subgroup.rayClassConductor_dvd_iff_forall_conductor_dvd` (SubgroupConductor/Basic.lean). Only the closure-under-gcd step is specific to each setting. The order-theoretic part is copied three times.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to `Modulus.wellFounded_dvd_and_ne` in RayClass/Modulus.lean:

theorem Modulus.min_dvd_of_gcd_mem {S : Set (Modulus K)} (hS : S.Nonempty) (hgcd : ∀ 𝔪 ∈ S, ∀ 𝔫 ∈ S, 𝔪.gcd 𝔫 ∈ S) {𝔫 : Modulus K} (h𝔫 : 𝔫 ∈ S) : wellFounded_dvd_and_ne.min S hS ∣ 𝔫.

Proof sketch. Let c be the minimum, so `c ∈ S` by `min_mem`. Then `c.gcd 𝔫 ∈ S`. By `not_lt_min`, `¬ (c.gcd 𝔫 ∣ c ∧ c.gcd 𝔫 ≠ c)`, and `gcd_dvd_left` gives `c.gcd 𝔫 = c`. Hence `c ∣ 𝔫` by `gcd_dvd_right`. This is exactly the moved block, with `U`-specific parts abstracted.

Rewritten use here: after the `refine`, the reverse direction becomes `Modulus.min_dvd_of_gcd_mem _ (fun 𝔞 h𝔞 𝔟 h𝔟 ↦ by show raySubgroup (𝔞.gcd 𝔟) ≤ U.toSubgroup; rw [raySubgroup_gcd]; exact sup_le h𝔞 h𝔟) h`, with the existence proof from the definition passed as the nonemptiness argument. The `show`/`unfold` is needed so that `U.ideleClassConductor` unfolds to the `min`. The same `raySubgroup_gcd`/`sup_le` step already appears at lines 256-258.

Hecke conductor: `conductor_dvd_iff` reverse direction becomes `Modulus.min_dvd_of_gcd_mem _ (fun _ ha _ hb ↦ mem_range_ofRayClassCharacter_gcd ha hb) h`.

Ray-class subgroup conductor: the reverse direction of `rayClassConductor_dvd_iff_forall_conductor_dvd` becomes `Modulus.min_dvd_of_gcd_mem _ (fun _ ha _ hb η hη ↦ Modulus.dvd_gcd (ha η hη) (hb η hη)) h`.
findings.benefit: Three copies of a delicate minimality argument become one proved lemma. Each conductor theorem then reduces to the closure of its set under gcd, which is the only mathematics specific to it. Future conductors of other objects, such as characters or norm groups, can reuse the lemma. A fix to the argument, for example when `Modulus.gcd` changes, is made in one place.
